title: Gate the UI brief's ork-only render sections by project, and keep a generic TUI route in ui.md for other projects. Both `## CLI text renders` and the new `## TUI renders` are written for every UI brief with no project check (`internal/engine/brief.go:231-238`). `roles_test.go:821-822` says "The UI pass runs in any project". ui.md:65-67 now sends every project's TUI views to that ork-only section, and the generic out-of-tree route is gone. A UI pass on another project would be told to run `go test ./internal/tui -run TestRenderTUIViews`, which does not exist there, and would then render nothing. The spec's step 6 asked for this wording, so the slice is not wrong. The cross-project gap is new. CONFIRMED by reading. PLAUSIBLE as to how often ork runs UI passes on other projects.

sections.heading: Why
sections.body:
The UI pass brief writes `## CLI text renders` and `## TUI renders` for every project (`internal/engine/brief.go:231-238`). Both name ork-only test commands: `go test ./internal/cli -run TestRenderCLIViews` and `go test ./internal/tui -run TestRenderTUIViews`. The `## Test run patterns` example (`internal/engine/brief.go:239`) names `TestRenderCLIViews` too. `internal/roles/prompts/ui.md:64-67` sends every project's TUI views to the ork-only section, so the generic route for other projects is gone. A UI pass in another project is told to run a test that does not exist there, and then renders nothing.

Owner decision (adj 662, `ui.brief-render-sections-gate`, detect-plus-fallback): write each render section only when the worktree has its render test. Otherwise write a short generic `## Renders` section that points at the project's `AGENTS.md` and docs, like the fallback at `internal/engine/brief.go:247`. Also folded in from S538 finding 1 (note of 2026-11-27, "One slice for both"): the brief's render sections tell the pass to run `-renders` with the renders directory as DIR, and the "copy the views" step goes. A read-only pass has no `cp`. The TUI flag already writes `NAME-80x24.txt` names.

Owner decisions, 2026-11-28: adj 662 (detect render tests, generic fallback), adj 667 (supersedes adj 508: CLI and TUI render commands write straight into the renders directory; S658 merged here) and adj 668 (round.go detects and sets BriefInput booleans).

sections.heading: Failing tests
sections.body:
In `internal/engine/brief_test.go`:
- TestUIPassBriefGatesRenderSectionsByWorktreeTests: a table over (`RenderCLI`, `RenderTUI`) = (true,true), (true,false), (false,true), (false,false). `## CLI text renders` is present only when `RenderCLI` is set. `## TUI renders` is present only when `RenderTUI` is set. The generic `## Renders` section is present in the other three rows, and absent when both are true. Find headings after the `\n# Brief\n` marker, because the prompt text also holds a `## Renders` heading.
- TestUIPassBriefFallbackRendersSection: with both fields false, the `## Renders` section names the project's `AGENTS.md` and docs. It contains neither `TestRenderCLIViews` nor `TestRenderTUIViews`, and no `-renders` command. The `## Test run patterns` section still has the `go -C WORKTREE test -run NAME PKG` form and has no `TestRenderCLIViews` example.
- TestUIPassBriefPointsRenderFlagAtRendersDir: with both fields set and `TempDir` `/state/role scratch/ui-1`, the CLI and TUI commands end with `-renders '/state/role scratch/ui-1/renders'`. Neither section says "Copy the views".
- TestUIPassBriefNamesTheRenderCommand, TestUIPassBriefNamesTheTUIRenderCommand, TestUIPassBriefNamesRenderFixtures and TestUIPassBriefNamesRunPatternRule (existing, changed): set `RenderCLI` and `RenderTUI` on the input. The expected `-renders` argument is the renders directory, not TMPDir. The TUI section no longer says "Copy the views".

In `internal/engine/renderdetect_test.go` (new):
- TestRenderTestsIn: in a temp worktree, `internal/cli/x_test.go` holding `func TestRenderCLIViews(` gives (cli true, tui false). `internal/tui/y_test.go` holding `func TestRenderTUIViews(` gives the reverse. Both present gives both true. An empty worktree, a missing `internal/` directory, and a directory that is a link give false.

In `internal/engine/uipass_test.go`:
- TestUIPassBriefHasFallbackRendersWithoutRenderTests: a round on `uiHarness` (its worktree has no render tests) sends the UI pass a brief with the `## Renders` fallback and without `## CLI text renders` or `## TUI renders`.

In `internal/cli/render_test.go`:
- TestUIPassBriefListsEveryRenderFixture (existing, changed): builds the input with `RenderCLI: true`. It reads the fixture list up to the new ending, ". ork's approval card lists every `.txt` file in the renders directory".

In `internal/roles/roles_test.go`:
- TestUIPromptNamesTheOutOfTreeRenderRoute (existing, changed): the Renders section also says that when the brief has no `## TUI renders` section, the pass follows the brief's `## Renders` section and the project's own tooling.

sections.heading: Implement
sections.body:
1. In `internal/engine/brief.go`, add `RenderCLI bool` and `RenderTUI bool` to `BriefInput`, with comments: the worktree has `TestRenderCLIViews` or `TestRenderTUIViews`.
2. Add `internal/engine/renderdetect.go` with `renderTestsIn(worktree string) (cli, tui bool)`. For `internal/cli` and `internal/tui`, read the directory. Skip entries that are not regular files and do not end in `_test.go`. Report a hit when a file holds `func TestRenderCLIViews(` or `func TestRenderTUIViews(`. A missing or unreadable directory counts as false. Start the file with the SPDX line.
3. In `internal/engine/round.go`, where `BriefInput` is built (line 644), set `RenderCLI` and `RenderTUI` from `renderTestsIn(rec.Worktree)` when the role is the UI pass.
4. In `BuildBrief` for `RoleUI`:
   - Write `## CLI text renders` only when `in.RenderCLI`, and `## TUI renders` only when `in.RenderTUI`. Keep the order CLI, TUI, Test run patterns.
   - Set DIR in both commands to `ShellWord(filepath.Join(in.TempDir, "renders"))`.
   - In the CLI text, replace "into your temp directory (named under Your files)" with "into the renders directory". Replace the closing "Copy the views you want on the approval card into the renders directory under the VIEW-80x24.txt names required by your prompt." with "ork's approval card lists every `.txt` file in the renders directory." The fixture list then ends with that sentence.
   - In the TUI text, drop the same copy sentence. Keep "A TUI view with no fixture is not rendered: say so in your report."
5. When either flag is false, write a short generic `## Renders` section after the render sections and before `## Test run patterns`. It says:
   - ork's render test for the CLI views, the TUI views, or both, is not in this worktree;
   - the pass finds how the project renders its views in its `AGENTS.md` and docs, and uses only that tooling;
   - the files go in the renders directory (give its path);
   - a view the tooling cannot render without changing the tree gets no file, and the report says so.
6. In the `## Test run patterns` text, name the `TestRenderCLIViews ./internal/cli` example only when `in.RenderCLI`. Otherwise drop the "for example ..." clause and keep the rest.
7. In `internal/roles/prompts/ui.md`, under Renders, keep "TUI views come from the TUI render command in the brief's `## TUI renders` section" and add ", when the brief has one". Add that when it has none, the pass follows the brief's `## Renders` section and the project's own tooling. Change the CLI line the same way. Keep the prompt ASCII, with no ork path (`TestUIPromptHasNoOrkPaths`).
8. Update `docs/design.md`, `docs/guide.md` and `AGENTS.md:103` to match:
   - DIR is the renders directory for both sections.
   - The "copies selected views" sentences go.
   - Each section appears only when the worktree has its render test, otherwise a generic `## Renders` section.
   - `AGENTS.md:103` says the role's renders directory as DIR.
   Keep `go test ./internal/tui -run TestRenderTUIViews -renders DIR` and the "No file is written without `-renders`." text unchanged, because `TestRenderTUIFixtureDocsListEveryFixture` and `TestRenderFixtureDocsListEveryFixture` read them.
9. Update the existing tests and add the new ones from Failing tests.
